correctness.rationale: For n>=2 and t disjoint deleted edges, every monochromatic fibre S of size a in K_n-M_t has same-color degree either a-1 (missing mate outside S) or a-2 (mate inside). Therefore all fibre sizes <=d+1 are legal; sizes >=d+3 forbidden; size d+2 is legal only if it is a disjoint union of (d+2)/2 whole missing-edge pairs, possible only for even d. Uniquely marking r exceptional color names and assigning s=h+1 matching edges to each gives binom(k,r)*t!/(s!^r(t-rs)!)*B_(d+1)(n-2sr,k-r). Every odd d has no exceptional fibre and equals the K_n polynomial; for even d, a nonzero difference begins at t>=s and has exact degree n-d-1 and leading coefficient binom(t,s), from r=1 and injective residual colors. The zero-vertex residual and k=0 cases are included. Independent direct graph/palette enumeration n=2..7 and k=1..3 for all allowed t,d agreed with the formula.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact defective-coloring invariant of the cocktail-party/matching-deleted clique family. The parity-blindness for all odd defect parameters, sharp first detectable even defect at t=h+1, and leading coefficient combinatorics distinguish graph-deletion influence on an entire polynomial family. These exact degeneracies and full generating formula are independently reusable in defective-coloring enumeration and graph-polynomial comparison, rather than a random tiny example.

limitations: Only deletions that form a matching are covered; an arbitrary deleted edge subgraph changes fibre degrees.
The k polynomial extension to complex values is formal and not a count of literal complex-color palettes; finite tests do not establish the general formula.
